claims.text: Cr-Hf pairs in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf exhibit strong attractive short-range ordering at low temperature, with negative Warren-Cowley parameters.
Chemical ordering between Cr and Hf in the cited W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf composition disappears near an order-disorder transition temperature of 1080 K.
Mo-Nb-Ta-W can form a BCC refractory alloy with and without chemical short-range order.
Specific refractory-alloy binary interactions, including W-V, have negative mixing enthalpies.
Negative mixing enthalpies of selected atomic pairs drive the proposed SRO in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf.
Annealing between 300 K and 800 K below the order-disorder transition will induce SRO in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf.
Rapid quenching after low-temperature annealing preserves the induced SRO at the thermal-conductivity measurement temperatures.
SRO consists of non-random local atomic correlations that produce local compositional fluctuations in a BCC lattice.
SRO clusters generate local strain fields.
SRO clusters modulate local interatomic force constants and mass variance.
The local force-constant and mass modulation caused by SRO increases the phonon scattering rate and decreases phonon mean free path.
SRO suppresses lattice thermal conductivity relative to a chemically identical random solid solution.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity suppression increases with the degree of SRO.
SRO-induced suppression should be most evident at intermediate temperatures, where defect scattering is more important relative to phonon-phonon scattering.
Thermal transport in the disordered baseline is governed primarily by mass-variance point-defect scattering and phonon-phonon Umklapp processes.
The proposed mechanism applies when SRO correlation lengths are comparable to or smaller than the dominant phonon wavelength.
Evolution from SRO to long-range precipitates would make phase-interface and grain-boundary scattering dominant.
SRO could reduce lattice anharmonicity and thereby reduce phonon-phonon scattering, opposing the proposed SRO-cluster scattering effect.
Strong intrinsic phonon-phonon scattering at elevated temperature may mask the SRO contribution in refractory alloys with high Debye temperatures.
A chemically matched disordered control and a 600 K, 24-hour SRO-annealed sample can be compared by TDTR while APT and HRTEM verify SRO and exclude precipitates.
